articles.title: Reliance and Meta Are Building India's First Hyperscale AI Data Centre. It Will Run on Seawater.
articles.excerpt: The 168-megawatt facility in Jamnagar marks Meta's first built-to-suit data centre in the country, powered by renewables and cooled with desalinated seawater — and Reliance will run the whole thing.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, Chairman of Reliance Industries, who called the deal a 'transformative moment' for India's digital infrastructure
articles.nri_angle: India hosting physical AI infrastructure for a $1.5 trillion American tech giant marks a shift from services to foundational computing. For NRIs tracking India's tech trajectory, this puts the country in the same conversation as the US, Ireland, and Singapore for hyperscale data centres.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zoho Just Built Its Own Server From Scratch. In Nagpur.
articles.excerpt: The Chennai-based SaaS giant spent five years designing a server platform in-house, with all intellectual property owned in India. It wants to cut AI inference costs by 30 percent and reduce dependence on foreign hardware.
articles.image_caption: Zoho Corporation headquarters in Chennai, the parent company behind the Nathu La server platform
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs in tech who have spent careers building infrastructure for American hyperscalers, Zoho designing competitive hardware in Nagpur — not Bangalore or an IIT incubator — is both validation and a statement about India's Tier 2 cities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. The Fight Is Not Over.
articles.excerpt: The ruling strikes down a charge that threatened to choke the pipeline Indian tech workers have built careers around. But the White House plans to appeal, and other restrictions remain firmly in place.
articles.image_caption: The US Capitol building in Washington, where Congress holds the exclusive authority to levy taxes that the judge ruled Trump overstepped
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals receive over 70% of all H-1B visas. The $100,000 fee threatened to fundamentally alter the economics of hiring Indian talent in America. With the Modi-Trump bilateral at the G7 just days away and H-1B visas on the agenda, the ruling adds a powerful card to New Delhi's hand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Slipped From the World's Fourth-Largest Economy to Sixth. The Opposition Just Published the Receipts.
articles.excerpt: Congress released a 76-page report card on Modi 3.0's second year. The findings: a record-low rupee, 8 per cent fuel hikes, capital flight, and a fiscal deficit heading toward 5 per cent.
articles.image_caption: The new Parliament building in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to 7% on Dollar Deposits. Here Is What Changed.
articles.excerpt: HDFC Bank, SBI, and smaller lenders have hiked rates by up to 300 basis points after the RBI agreed to absorb all hedging costs. The window closes in September.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Twenty-Four Indian Sailors Were on a Tanker Hit by a Suspected US Missile Off Oman. Two Are Missing.
articles.excerpt: The Settebello, operated by an India-based company, was struck 20 nautical miles off Sohar. The Omani Navy responded to the distress call.
articles.image_caption: A chemical and oil products tanker at sea
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The EB-2 Green Card Queue for Indians Just Slammed Shut. It Won't Reopen Until October.
articles.excerpt: The State Department marked EB-2 India 'unavailable' after the final action date retrogressed by more than ten months. Hundreds of thousands of H-1B professionals are stuck in place until the new fiscal year.
articles.image_caption: USCIS headquarters groundbreaking ceremony in Camp Springs, Maryland
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Mapped 197 Districts That Could Starve if the Monsoon Fails. The Government Has a Plan.
articles.excerpt: Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveiled state-by-state contingency plans as Pacific temperatures crossed the El Niño threshold. Some scientists warn this could become the strongest El Niño ever recorded.
articles.image_caption: Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan at a government event in 2025
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Running Out of Cancer Drugs. The Iran War Made Platinum Too Expensive.
articles.excerpt: Cisplatin and carboplatin shortages are forcing patients to hunt across cities for their next dose as drugmakers halt production over price caps that no longer cover costs.
articles.image_caption: The All India Institute of Medical Sciences in New Delhi, where oncologists are rationing platinum-based chemotherapy drugs (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: All India Organisation of Chemists and Druggists

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Want a US Visa Interview in 10 Days? That Will Be $750 Extra.
articles.excerpt: The State Department is launching a premium fast-track service for B1/B2 visa applicants starting July 1, just in time for the FIFA World Cup. For Indians facing 16-month wait times, it is both a lifeline and a tax on urgency.
articles.image_caption: The US Embassy in New Delhi, where Indian visa applicants face some of the longest wait times in the world
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Has Now Served Longer Than Nehru. No Elected Indian PM Has Lasted This Long.
articles.excerpt: With 4,399 consecutive days in office, Narendra Modi surpasses Jawaharlal Nehru's post-independence record — the first PM to hold power through three unbroken democratic mandates.
articles.image_caption: Official portrait of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, now India's longest-serving continuously elected PM
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Just Hit US Bases in Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain. India Has 8 Million Reasons to Worry.
articles.excerpt: The biggest military escalation since the April ceasefire puts India's Gulf diaspora, oil supply chain and economic recovery on a razor's edge.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, through which 8 million Indian workers in the Gulf region depend on stability now threatened by the Iran-US military exchange (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Inflation Is About to Breach 4% for the First Time in 15 Months. The War Bill Has Arrived.
articles.excerpt: Four fuel price hikes in May, a heatwave that crushed vegetable supply and a weakening rupee are ending India's longest low-inflation streak in years.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai — the central bank faces its first above-target inflation reading in 15 months (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Companies Worth $4 Trillion Are About to Go Public. Thousands of Indian Engineers Hold the Lottery Tickets.
articles.excerpt: SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI will list within weeks of each other. For Indian tech workers with ESOP stakes, this is the biggest liquidity event of a generation.
articles.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon rocket launch — the company is expected to go public this week at a .77 trillion valuation, one of three mega-IPOs with thousands of Indian engineer shareholders (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Fertiliser Ministry Wants to Double Its Subsidy Budget. The Fiscal Year Is Three Months Old.
articles.excerpt: With global fertiliser prices surging and El Niño threatening the monsoon, New Delhi is already scrambling to contain a cascading food security crisis that could touch every Indian household.
articles.image_caption: Rice cultivation in India — the country's agricultural sector depends heavily on fertiliser subsidies for food security
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Fell to Seventh in the Global Stock Market Rankings. AI Took Its Place.
articles.excerpt: Taiwan and South Korea overtook India in rapid succession as the global AI investment boom bypassed the world's fastest-growing major economy. Foreign investors have pulled $26.4 billion from Indian equities in 2026.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, the oldest stock exchange in Asia
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Inflation Is About to Hit a Three-Year High. Every Indian Immigrant Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: May's consumer price index is expected to show the sharpest annual increase since April 2023, driven by soaring energy costs from the Middle East war. Real wages are falling, and the Fed is unlikely to offer relief.
articles.image_caption: The Eccles Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Annamalai Has Left the BJP. He Wants to Build Tamil Nadu's Next Political Party From Scratch.
articles.excerpt: The former IPS officer and ex-state BJP president resigned after 18 months of disagreements with the central leadership. His new movement will contest the 2031 assembly elections.
articles.image_caption: K. Annamalai during his statewide padayatra across Tamil Nadu
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Is About to Become the Biggest IPO in History. Indian Tech Workers Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: With $250 billion in demand and a $1.77 trillion valuation, the SpaceX listing will reshape the market conditions that underpin Indian American wealth in tech.
articles.image_caption: Elon Musk, founder and CEO of SpaceX, which is set to go public at a $1.77 trillion valuation
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Telangana Man Delivered Pizzas to a Vacant Apartment in Philadelphia. He Was Shot Dead.
articles.excerpt: Anshul Kuncha, 28, was lured to an empty housing unit by what his family calls a fake order. Nothing was stolen. The Indian diaspora is asking hard questions about safety in America.
articles.image_caption: The Philadelphia skyline, where Anshul Kuncha worked and was fatally shot during a pizza delivery

sources.label: Consulate General of India New York

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Approved a $428 Million Deal to Keep India's Apaches and Howitzers Running.
articles.excerpt: Boeing, Lockheed Martin, and BAE Systems will sustain India's most critical American-made weapons platforms. The deal deepens a defence relationship that is no longer aspirational.
articles.image_caption: An AH-64D Apache Longbow attack helicopter, the same platform operated by the Indian Army
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Gold Tariff Hike Was Supposed to Shrink the Trade Deficit. It Built a Smuggling Empire Instead.
articles.excerpt: Illegal gold imports could hit 100 metric tons this year as grey-market discounts exceed $200 an ounce. Banks, refiners, and the legal market are caught in the crossfire.
articles.image_caption: Gold ingots and bars at a bank vault display
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Jet Fuel Stabilisation Fund Just Went Live. Airlines Are Not Signing Up.
articles.excerpt: The ₹10,000 crore aviation fuel fund fixes ATF at ₹115 per litre for three years. But a 10% price hike today and a three-year lock-in have carriers hesitating.
articles.image_caption: An IndiGo aircraft at an Indian airport
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: El Niño Just Crossed the Drought Threshold. India's Monsoon Is Already 18% Short.
articles.excerpt: Sea surface temperatures hit +0.81°C — just above the El Niño line. IMD has downgraded the monsoon forecast to 90% of normal. For 800 million Indians who depend on rain-fed agriculture, the timing could not be worse.
articles.image_caption: A flooded paddy field in Raichur, Karnataka during monsoon season
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Germany and France Just Scrapped the Transit Visa for Indians. Here's Why It Matters.
articles.excerpt: Indian passport holders can now connect through Frankfurt, Munich, and Paris without extra paperwork — a quiet win that opens up competitive long-haul routing across Europe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Walked Away From the Table. India's Oil Clock Just Started Ticking Faster.
articles.excerpt: Tehran suspended ceasefire talks after Israel struck Tyre, the US hit Qeshm island, and global oil inventories fell toward their lowest levels since 2003.
articles.image_caption: US Navy vessels patrol near the Strait of Hormuz
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World Is Running Out of Oil Reserves. India Cannot Afford to Wait.
articles.excerpt: The EIA warned that OECD oil inventories are headed to their lowest levels since 2003. India, which imports 85% of its crude, faces an existential squeeze.
articles.image_caption: India imports 85% of its crude oil, making it acutely vulnerable to global supply shocks
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A New Bill Wants to Kill the H-1B Green Card Pipeline. Every Indian Worker in America Should Read It.
articles.excerpt: Rep. Chip Roy's American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act would end dual intent, eliminate OPT, and cut the visa to two years. If it passes, the rules of the game change entirely.
articles.image_caption: Rep. Chip Roy of Texas, sponsor of the American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US House Just Cleared a $70 Billion Bill to Fund ICE Through the End of Trump's Term.
articles.excerpt: The legislation passed its procedural vote 213-211. No new oversight. No reforms. And a fully funded enforcement machine that will define the next three years for every immigrant in America.
articles.image_caption: The US Capitol in Washington, DC, where the House voted on the immigration enforcement bill
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Downed a US Apache Over the Strait of Hormuz. India's Fragile Oil Lifeline Just Got More Fragile.
articles.excerpt: A Shahed drone reportedly struck the helicopter. Both pilots survived, but the ceasefire Trump promised is unravelling — and India's $90-a-barrel nightmare is back on the table.
articles.image_caption: A US Army AH-64 Apache attack helicopter in flight
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven Indian Workers Died on a Dubai Highway. A Truck Stopped. A Bus Didn't.
articles.excerpt: A minibus carrying workers slammed into a stalled truck on Emirates Road. Seven are dead, nine injured. The Indian Consulate is at the hospital.
articles.image_caption: A multilane highway in Dubai, similar to Emirates Road where the fatal crash occurred
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRI Remittances Hit $43.5 Billion in One Quarter. The Gulf Crisis Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: India posted a surprise current account surplus in Q4 FY26 — and the money flowing home from frightened workers in West Asia is what made it possible.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Heads to France and Slovakia This Week. It Is India's First PM Visit to Bratislava Ever.
articles.excerpt: The six-day European tour covers the G7 summit in Evian, a startup showcase in Nice, and the first Indian prime ministerial visit to Slovakia since the country's independence in 1993.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Will Have Half a Million AI Agents Within Three Years. Hiring Will Shrink.
articles.excerpt: Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran told shareholders that AI workers will match TCS's human headcount — and that the days of mass IT hiring are over.
articles.image_caption: Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran at a corporate event
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US and Iran Say a Deal Is Days Away. India Needs It More Than Anyone at the Table.
articles.excerpt: A ceasefire framework that reopens the Strait of Hormuz would begin to reverse the worst energy supply crisis India has faced in years — but the gap between 'largely negotiated' and 'signed' has been wide before.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world's oil transits
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eight Workers Burned Alive at Vizag Steel Plant. A Crane Carrying Molten Iron Collapsed.
articles.excerpt: The deadliest industrial accident at India's flagship steel plant in years has reignited questions about ageing equipment, safety lapses, and the cost of privatisation delays
articles.image_caption: Entrance to the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant in Andhra Pradesh
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Delhi Hotel Was Licensed for Six Rooms. It Was Running Twenty-Five. Twenty-Two People Are Dead.
articles.excerpt: The Malviya Nagar fire has killed 22 people, including 13 foreign nationals, and exposed a fire safety crisis in the capital's unregulated hospitality sector
articles.image_caption: South Delhi's Malviya Nagar area, where a licensed-for-six hotel was running 25 rooms when fire killed 22 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Congress Tells Modi: You Pocketed the Cheap Oil. Now Swallow the Expensive Kind.
articles.excerpt: A 76-page opposition report says India has slipped to the world's sixth-largest economy, the rupee has hit a record low, and the government is passing the Iran war's costs to consumers
articles.image_caption: A Bharat Petroleum fuel station in India
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Cut the Cost of Bringing Dollars Home. NRIs, This One Is for You.
articles.excerpt: A concessional forex swap at half the market rate, leverage on NRI deposits, and a $50–70 billion inflow target — India's central bank is pulling every lever to defend the rupee.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Sent a Delegation to Russia Last Month. It Came Back Talking About Coal Mines.
articles.excerpt: SAIL and NMDC are exploring acquisitions of coking coal assets in Russia and boosting nickel imports — a quiet but significant pivot in India's raw materials strategy.
articles.image_caption: Molten metal pouring in a steel mill blast furnace
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Hormuz Blockade Has a Hole. Nearly 3 Million Barrels a Day Are Slipping Through.
articles.excerpt: Ghost tankers with transponders off, Qatari LNG carriers paying tolls, and clandestine dark transits — the supposedly sealed Strait of Hormuz is leaking oil. For India, it may be the difference between a crisis and a catastrophe.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker sailing on the open sea
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. Indian Tech Exhaled.
articles.excerpt: Judge Leo Sorokin called it an unauthorized tax. Only 85 companies had paid it. The White House says it will appeal — but for now, the most punitive visa fee in US history is dead.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. federal courthouse — where a Massachusetts judge struck down the Trump administration's 00,000 H-1B fee (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA's Chief Just Arrived in India. An Indian Astronaut Is Headed to the ISS.
articles.excerpt: Bill Nelson's India visit cements the most ambitious phase of US-India space collaboration yet — an ISS mission, a Goddard Award for Chandrayaan-3, and a commercial space station offer on the table.
articles.image_caption: NASA Administrator Bill Nelson, who arrived in India this week for meetings with ISRO leadership
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and the US Expect a Trade Deal Within Weeks. The Tariff Threat Still Looms.
articles.excerpt: A two-way agreement is on the table, but India wants a written guarantee: no future tariffs after the deal is signed. Washington has not yet agreed.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who is leading trade negotiations with Washington
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Moved the EB-2 India Green Card Line Backward by 10 Months. Thousands Are Stuck Again.
articles.excerpt: The June 2026 visa bulletin pushed the EB-2 India final action date to September 2013 — erasing nearly a year of progress for Indian professionals waiting for permanent residency.
articles.image_caption: A US Citizenship and Immigration Services facility processes visa applications
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Biscuit Packet Is Smaller. Your Petrol Bill Is Higher. India Inc Is Passing the War to You.
articles.excerpt: From Hindustan Unilever to Maruti Suzuki, Indian companies are hiking prices and shrinking product sizes as the Iran war drives up oil, freight, and raw material costs across the board.
articles.image_caption: An Indian consumer goods store stocked with household products and groceries
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Goldilocks Economy Is Over. The Iran War Broke It.
articles.excerpt: GDP growth projected to slow to 6.7% in FY27 as oil at $97, a weak rupee, and fertiliser shortages create overlapping supply shocks that the RBI cannot simply cut its way out of.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, the nerve centre of India's monetary policy response
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A US Fighter Jet Hit an Oil Tanker in the Gulf of Oman. All 24 Sailors on Board Were Indian.
articles.excerpt: The Palau-flagged MT Marivex tried to run the American blockade four times before an F/A-18 from the USS Abraham Lincoln disabled it. Omani authorities rescued the entire Indian crew.
articles.image_caption: An F/A-18 Super Hornet launches from the USS Abraham Lincoln, the carrier whose jet disabled the MT Marivex
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Indian Air Force Will Fly NEET Papers to 18 Military Hubs. The Paper Setters Are Already in Lockdown.
articles.excerpt: After the May exam was cancelled over a leaked paper that matched 120 questions, India is treating the June 21 re-exam like a military operation. For 22.79 lakh students, a second chance hinges on a chain of custody that now runs through the armed forces.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Air Force transport aircraft — IAF planes will deliver NEET question papers to 18 military hubs nationwide
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Opposition Just Met in Delhi. Kharge Told Them the Economy Is Broken and Modi's Government Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: The INDIA bloc's latest show of unity comes as inflation crosses the RBI's target, fuel prices climb for the fourth time in three weeks, and the opposition tries to build on a rare Lok Sabha victory.
articles.image_caption: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addresses party leaders at the INDIA bloc meeting in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
